Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

quite adverb

completely

also completely, entirely, absolutely, not quite, quite right, simply (absolutely), totally, perfectly (perfectly clear, perfectly well), good and proper

classical

Cic. Att. 13.6.2: plānē bene, “quite right”
Cic. Att. 12.37.1: plānē bellē sē habēre
Phaedr. 3.7.26: nōn plānē est
Traupman 107: I simply don’t know what he is thinking of, jam plānē quid cōgitet nesciō

plānē

adverb

quite, completely, entirely

Nōn plānē is “not quite”. Traupman gives admodum for “quite” and parum, “too little”, for “not quite” (p. 367).

Other words

  • prōrsus (prōrsum) — absolutely, utterly; with a negative, at all

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.14: ita prōrsus exīstimō (Lewis & Short); Ter. Heaut. 776: nam prōrsum nihil intelligō; Traupman 267

  • omnīnō — altogether, entirely; with a negative, at all

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.42: tamquam omnīnō sine animō sint; Traupman 267

  • admodum — quite, very; with numbers, fully, just about

    adverb, often after its word · also used · classical · Traupman 367; Liv. 21.36.2: in pedum mīlle admodum altitūdinem

Examples

  • quod reliquōs cohērēdēs convēnistī, plānē bene

    as for your meeting the other co-heirs, quite rightCic. Att. 13.6.2

  • age, sī quō abīre est animus, est licentia? — nōn plānē est, inquit.

    “Come now, if you want to go off somewhere, are you allowed?” “Not quite,” he said.Phaedr. 3.7.25–26

  • in here neque E plānē neque I audītur

    in here you hear neither quite an e nor quite an iQuint. 1.4.8

  • nōn omnīnō

    simply notTraupman 379

  • plānē et probē

    good and proper, thoroughlyTraupman 322

See also quite.
